---
title: "My first weeks in MDS"
author: "Kade Schneider"
date: 2026-09-08
---

![Figure 1](MDSfirstweeks.png)

I'm in the middle of my second week of MDSCL and thus far I'm very pleased with how it's gone for me. Orientation rattled me a bit with every other sentence coming out of someone's mouth pertaining to the rigor of this program-- not that I disagree with them--, but I think the workflow is very in tune with what I was looking for.

I have had far less busy times in my life where I feel like my brain was always swarming with thoughts about the few things I was keeping track of all day long. My brain likes to be on top of things and organized, so without a way to put a cap on things, my brain is always worrying. Though MDSCL has required long hours, when I finally finish, I can go home and take the evening or weekend off-- not just physically but also mentally (see Figure 1). The workflow very much allows for a separation between school and not school that really lets me appreciate my time off without having me worrying at all times. And that is the time off that I believe will let me recharge and prevent any burnout this year. Fingers crossed. I know I'm not in the thick of it yet, but I'm hopeful.

Otherwise, the part that surprised me the most is how great the people have been. Not that I expected them to be unfriendly, but the sense of camaraderie I feel with everyone in my classes and labs is unmatched. The shared adversity/trauma bonding has made it really easy to befriend classmates and aid one another through the program.
